methodology.esco_version: 1.2.1 (official ESCO current version shown on ESCO site; ENISA crosswalk references ESCO v1.2)
methodology.ecsf_baseline: Role Profiles published 2022; ENISA says ECSF is currently under revision and a public consultation is planned for end 2026.
methodology.rule: Only ESCO codes and relationships explicitly listed in the ENISA↔ESCO crosswalk are reproduced. They are not inserted into the canonical M-TIER classification_crosswalk until the ESCO concept URI, version, tasks and reviewer are recorded.
methodology.isco08: No ISCO-08 unit-group codes assigned in this checkpoint; classification requires review of official group definitions and the actual task bundle.
methodology.onet: No O*NET SOC codes assigned in this checkpoint; US occupational context and task scope require separate controlled review.

overlap_decisions.decision: Keep both drafts for now. Engineer = design, integration, automation and technical governance; specialist = operational identity lifecycle, access requests and periodic access review. Reassess against real job descriptions from at least three different labour markets before counting them as distinct occupations.

Keep the coordinator record in the data as a provisional functional variant, but exclude it from the count of distinct occupations until evidence shows autonomous hiring demand and distinct accountability.

source_updates.supports: Official relationship types and ESCO codes for ECSF roles.
Baseline ECSF role profiles and their tasks, skills and knowledge.
Versioned NICE work roles and Task, Knowledge and Skill components.
ESCO occupation structure, version and relationship to ISCO-08.
Official ISCO-08 group definitions and correspondence tables; no code assigned in this checkpoint.

limitations: The official ENISA crosswalk is an ESCO↔ECSF relationship table, not an automatic M-TIER occupation crosswalk.
A direct ESCO↔ECSF relationship does not by itself validate a M-TIER profile mapping.
No national licensing, education, certification, salary or employment-demand claims are made.
The NICE Framework describes work roles, tasks, knowledge and skills; a work role is not automatically a job or occupation.
Professional review remains required for the two overlap decisions and all final occupation mappings.

Deux correspondances ESCO exactes ont ensuite été confirmées au niveau des concepts par le crosswalk ENISA et inscrites dans le registre canonique v3.0 : Ethical hacker (2529.4) et Cyber incident responder (2529.7). Cette confirmation ne remplace pas la revue experte indépendante des fiches M-TIER.
